11 A square board, of side length x, hangs freely from a nail P, as shown.
The board has uniform thickness and is made from material of uniform density.
Q
x
P
2x

A second square board, of side length 2x, is made of the same material and has the same
thickness as the original board. This second board is then hung from a nail Q. Nails P and Q are
at the same height.
What is the vertical distance between the positions of the centres of gravity of the two boards?
A
0
B
x
C
x
D
2
x
2

hints: Notice each square hangs from a corner, so its centre of gravity lies vertically below the nail along the diagonal.
For a uniform square the centre is at the intersection of the diagonals, so the nail-to-centre distance is half of one diagonal.
Compare half the diagonal of side $x$ with half the diagonal of side $2x$ using diagonal $= \text{side} \times \sqrt{2}$.
walkthrough: Each board is uniform, so its centre of gravity is at its geometric centre where the diagonals cross.
When hung freely, the centre lies vertically below the nail, so the depth below the nail equals half the diagonal length.
For a square of side $s$, diagonal $= s\sqrt{2}$ by Pythagoras, so depth $= s\sqrt{2}/2 = s/\sqrt{2}$.
Small board: depth below P is $x/\sqrt{2}$. Large board: depth below Q is $2x/\sqrt{2} = x\sqrt{2}$.
P and Q are at the same height, so vertical separation $= x\sqrt{2} - x/\sqrt{2} = (2x - x)/\sqrt{2} = x/\sqrt{2}$.

A.explanation: The two diagonals are different lengths, so the centres cannot hang at the same depth below nails at the same height.

B.explanation: Half-diagonal difference is $x\sqrt{2} - x/\sqrt{2} = x/\sqrt{2}$, which is the vertical separation of the centres.

C.explanation: This is the difference in side length, not the difference in half the diagonal distance from nail to centre.

D.explanation: This is the nail-to-centre distance for the $2x$ board alone, not the difference between the two boards.
